description.summary: Android task windows that behave like native windows

protocol.description:
This protocol lets the CrownOS Android runtime describe the Android task behind each of its xdg_toplevels, so the compositor can treat the window like any other application window and still offer what Android apps need: a Back button, a fixed size for apps that cannot resize, and the app's own title color.
Everything else uses standard protocols. Size comes from xdg_toplevel configure, minimum and maximum size from xdg_toplevel.set_min_size and set_max_size, identity from xdg_toplevel.set_app_id, which is "waydroid." followed by the Android package name, and visibility from the xdg_toplevel suspended state.
The compositor only advertises the manager to the CrownOS Android runtime: the hwcomposer connection that comes through the runtime's security context, and the runtime daemon itself.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_android_shell_manager_v1

description.summary: attach Android task details to toplevels

interface.description: A global the CrownOS Android runtime binds to describe its windows.

entry.name: already_extended
entry.summary: the xdg_toplevel already has a crownos_android_toplevel_v1

entry.name: not_allowed
entry.summary: this client may not make placeholders

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects created through the manager stay valid.

request.name: get_android_toplevel

description.summary: describe the Android task behind a toplevel

request.description: Creates the Android extension of an xdg_toplevel. A toplevel has at most one; asking for a second is the already_extended error. Send it before the toplevel's first commit with a buffer, so the compositor can place the window as an Android window from the start.

request.name: mark_placeholder

description.summary: mark a toplevel as the stand-in for a launching app

request.description:
Marks a toplevel as the splash window of an Android app that is still starting. When a toplevel with the same app_id maps from the Android runtime, the compositor gives it the placeholder's place, size and state, then sends xdg_toplevel.close to the placeholder. The compositor ignores the mark after 120 seconds.
Only the runtime daemon may send this; anyone else gets the not_allowed error.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: app_id of the window to wait for

interface.name: crownos_android_toplevel_v1

description.summary: the Android task behind one toplevel

interface.description: Describes one Android task window. Destroying it does not affect the xdg_toplevel; the window simply loses its Android extras.

entry.name: fixed
entry.summary: the app cannot resize; keep the size it asks for and float the window

entry.name: aspect
entry.summary: the app resizes but keeps the ratio from set_aspect

description.summary: drop the Android extras of the window

request.name: set_task

description.summary: the Android task this window shows

request.description: task_id is Android's task id, stable for the life of the task. package is the Android package name. Both are double-buffered and applied on the next xdg_surface commit.

request.name: set_resize_lock

description.summary: how the window may be resized

request.description: Double-buffered, applied on the next commit. The default is none.

request.name: set_aspect

description.summary: width to height ratio kept by the aspect lock

request.description: Double-buffered. Zero for either value clears the ratio.

request.name: set_title_color

description.summary: the app's primary color for the title bar

request.description: 0xAARRGGBB. An alpha of zero means the app has no color and the compositor uses its own. Double-buffered.

event.name: back

description.summary: the user pressed Back for this window

event.description: Sent when the user activates the title bar's Back button or the compositor's Back shortcut while this window has focus.
